newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Bolivia put new extradition treaty into force.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Bolivia put new extradition treaty into force.

text.p: The United States and Bolivia on Thursday put into force a new extradition treaty that will make it easier to prosecute drug traffickers, a State Department spokesman said.
The new treaty, which took several years to negotiate, replaced another one that had been in effect since the year 1900, spokesman Glyn Davies said.
"This agreement is significant because, unlike its predecessor, it requires both countries to extradite their own nationals for serious criminal offences," he added.
Bolivia is one of the world's largest producers of coca leaves, from which cocaine is extracted.
The United States has longed pressed Bolivia and other Latin American countries like Colombia and Mexico to allow the extradition of their nationals on drug charges.

Mexico started turning over a few suspected traffickers to the United States this year. Colombia has a constitutional ban on the extradition of its nationals, although its Congress is currently considering a bill to scrap that restriction.
